item.title: EDITORIAL: It’s Time for African Americans to Reignite the Activism That Fueled the Civil Rights Movement
item.description: In order to combat the surge of white supremacy, Americans must become active at the local level and follow the same blueprint that led to the Supreme Court's ruling in Brown v. Board, the passage of the Voting Rights Act, and the election of a wave of African Americans in Congress and in mayoral races across the country. The post EDITORIAL: It’s Time for African Americans to Reignite the Activism That Fueled the Civil Rights Movement appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: VIEWPOINTS

item.title: Every Child Deserves A Classroom: Addressing Ghana’s Education Gap
item.description: Prince Anthony Bart-Appiah is partnering with the Ghana Education Trust Fund to launch the Every Child Deserves a Classroom initiative, which encourages people of African descent to visit Ghana, adopt trees, and help build schools to close the country's education gap. item.title: Local Leaders Work to Prevent Federal Interference as Thousands Protest ICE-Involved Fatal Shootings in Minneapolis
item.description: Local leaders are calling for justice for Renee Good and Alex Pretti, who were fatally shot by ICE officers in Minneapolis, and an end to the Trump administration's federal interference in Minnesota and other cities. item.title: AG Orders Closure of Youth Charities After Funds Raised by Children Never Reached Programs
item.description: Two nonprofit organizations, Maryland Youth Club and Virginia Youth Club, have been permanently shut down after a joint investigation found that they had used children from low-income neighborhoods to generate hundreds of thousands of dollars that never reached charitable programs. The post AG Orders Closure of Youth Charities After Funds Raised by Children Never Reached Programs appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: As Longtime Del. Norton Retires, the Fight for D.C.’s Scattered Continues
item.description: Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.) has been a champion of D.C. statehood and advocate of D.C. residents, but there is still much work to be done to ensure that incarcerated D.C. residents are placed in federal facilities in close proximity to the District, as evidenced by the death of David Blakeney, who died in a Pennsylvania prison due to neglect. The post As Longtime Del. Norton Retires, the Fight for D.C.’s Scattered Continues appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: With New Upgrade, Leckie Education Campus Moves Into the Future
item.description: Leckie Education Campus has completed a two-story addition, providing students with new classrooms, science lab, dining room, and other amenities, as well as improved accessibility and security, and was designed with input from students, faculty, and staff.
